request.system: You are an experienced audio electronics technician diagnosing a unit on the bench. Exactly one component has failed. Use the measure tool to take readings (each costs effort; stay within the budget), then call diagnose with your ranked list of the most likely faults, naming them exactly as in the fault list. Think like a technician: compare readings with the healthy values and their tolerances.

messages.content:
Circuit: Block 1 - Power supply (LV regulator + HV B+ chain). Low-voltage rail: rectified 18 Vrms secondary into a 2200 uF reservoir, then a discrete series regulator (16 V zener reference, 2N3904 pass transistor) giving about +15.2 V. High-voltage rail: rectified ~200 Vrms secondary into a 47 uF reservoir with a 220k bleeder, then a two-section RC filter chain giving about 254 V B+. Mains wiring, transformer, rectifier diodes and fuse are out of scope.

Stages: psu_lv = LV supply and regulator; psu_hv = HV B+ supply and filter chain

Parts:
- C101: electrolytic 2200u (stage psu_lv)
- R102: resistor 1k (stage psu_lv)
- D101: zener 16 V (stage psu_lv)
- C102: electrolytic 47u (stage psu_lv)
- Q101: bjt 2N3904 (stage psu_lv)
- D102: diode 1N4148 (stage psu_lv)
- C103: electrolytic 220u (stage psu_lv)
- R103: resistor 2.2k (stage psu_lv)
- C104: electrolytic 47u (stage psu_hv)
- R104: resistor 220k (stage psu_hv)
- R105: resistor 10k (stage psu_hv)
- C105: electrolytic 22u (stage psu_hv)
- R106: resistor 22k (stage psu_hv)
- C106: electrolytic 22u (stage psu_hv)

Netlist of the healthy circuit (SPICE; node names as in the test points):
* Differential reference circuit - Block 1: power supply (standalone)
* ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
* Original generic design written for this project (not derived from any
* commercial schematic). Two rails:
*   LV: bridge-rectified 18 Vrms secondary -> 2200 uF reservoir -> discrete
*       series regulator (1N4745A 16 V zener reference + 2N3904 pass transistor;
*       about 22 mA load, 0.2 W dissipation)
*   HV: rectified ~200 Vrms secondary -> 47 uF reservoir -> two-section RC filter
*       chain -> ~250 V B+ for the triode stage.
* Model boundary: the transformer, rectifier diodes and fuse are mains-side /
* out of scope. Each rectifier is represented by a quasi-static average model
* (B source) isolated from the ripple path by a large inductor, plus an injected
* 120 Hz ripple current of amplitude 2*Idc (the fundamental of the rectifier
* charging-pulse train). VHUMREF carries AC 1 only during the hum analysis.
* See docs/hand_calcs.md section "Power supply" for the derivation and limits.
* Run standalone: ngspice -b circuits/psu/psu.cir
* ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
.include ../lib/devices.lib

* ---- LV rectifier (quasi-static model; parameter nodes pk_lv, cres_lv) ----
VPK_LV pk_lv 0 DC 24.06
VCRES_LV cres_lv 0 DC 2200e-6
BRECT_LV rect_lv 0 V = max(V(pk_lv) - I(VSENS_LV)*(1.5 + 1/(240*V(cres_lv))), 0.6366*V(pk_lv) - I(VSENS_LV)*1.5)
LRECT_LV rect_lv rect_lv_l 10
VSENS_LV rect_lv_l vunreg DC 0
BRIP_LV 0 vunreg I = 2*V(humref)*I(VSENS_LV)
VHUMREF humref 0 DC 0 AC 0

* ---- LV reservoir and series regulator ----
C101 vunreg c101_esr 2200u
RESR_C101 c101_esr 0 0.072
R102 vunreg vz 1k
XD101 0 vz pvz_d101 ZENER_1N4745A
VPVZ_D101 pvz_d101 0 DC 14.6
C102 vz c102_esr 47u
RESR_C102 c102_esr 0 3.95
Q101 vunreg vz vreg Q2N3904
D102 vreg vunreg D1N4148
C103 vreg c103_esr 220u
RESR_C103 c103_esr 0 0.84
R103 vreg 0 2.2k

* ---- HV rectifier (quasi-static model; parameter nodes pk_hv, cres_hv) ----
VPK_HV pk_hv 0 DC 282
VCRES_HV cres_hv 0 DC 47e-6
BRECT_HV rect_hv 0 V = max(V(pk_hv) - I(VSENS_HV)*(150 + 1/(240*V(cres_hv))), 0.6366*V(pk_hv) - I(VSENS_HV)*150)
LRECT_HV rect_hv rect_hv_l 100
VSENS_HV rect_hv_l hv1 DC 0
BRIP_HV 0 hv1 I = 2*V(humref)*I(VSENS_HV)

* ---- HV reservoir, bleeder and RC filter chain ----
C104 hv1 c104_esr 47u
RESR_C104 c104_esr 0 5.64
R104 hv1 0 220k
R105 hv1 hv2 10k
C105 hv2 c105_esr 22u
RESR_C105 c105_esr 0 12.06
R106 hv2 bplus 22k
C106 bplus c106_esr 22u
RESR_C106 c106_esr 0 12.06

* ---- Fixtures (standalone bench test only): dummy loads ----
RLOAD_LV vreg 0 1k
RLOAD_HV bplus 0 300k

.control
set noaskquit
op
print v(vunreg) v(vz) v(vreg) v(hv1) v(hv2) v(bplus)
.endc
.end

Test points:
- TP1: node vunreg, Unregulated LV rail (stage psu_lv)
- TP2: node vz, Zener reference (stage psu_lv)
- TP3: node vreg, Regulated +15 V rail (stage psu_lv)
- TP4: node hv1, HV reservoir (stage psu_hv) (HIGH VOLTAGE)
- TP5: node hv2, HV filter node (stage psu_hv) (HIGH VOLTAGE)
- TP6: node bplus, B+ to triode stage (stage psu_hv) (HIGH VOLTAGE)

Customer complaint: Channel strip in for service, single channel, rack mount. Meter shows incorrect DC figures throughout the high-voltage supply. Marginal but repeatable. Please advise.

Diagnose the unit. (Session 3 of 3.)

content.text: I'll start by measuring the three HV node DC voltages.

content.thinking: All HV readings run about 5% high but remain in tolerance, and the filter-resistor ratios look normal, so the whole rail has shifted up, most likely from R104 drifting or C104 losing capacitance. I'm checking ripple at TP4 next to tell those apart.

The R104 resistor is the likeliest cause of the 294.8 V reading, since the rectifier math and the load estimates don't explain the rise from ripple, bleeder, or R104 in a smaller value. I'm lifting R104 to check it next.

tools.name: diagnose
tools.description: Finish with a ranked list of fault names.

content.thinking: R104 is within tolerance and the remaining effort is 14, too little for more HV lifts. The shift hits all three nodes, so it's upstream of TP4, and I suspect C104 cap_loss; I'm going with that.
